title: Flatness of finite locally free étale coefficient sheaves
statement: Let Λ be a finite commutative ring, X a scheme, L a sheaf of Λ-modules on the small etale site of X, and t a natural number. Use the canonical constant-ring sheaf and its coefficient realization [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. If this realization of L is finite locally free of rank t, then L is a flat object of the category of fixed-ring sheaves of Λ-modules: tensoring by L on either side is exact. Rank zero and the zero coefficient ring are allowed.

source.place: Section Flat modules, lemmas flatness-sheafification-refined and flatness-local; local finite free bases.

proof.text: The associated-module-sheaf adjunction unit identifies the original fixed-ring sheaf L with the restriction to constant scalars of its realization M: the underlying abelian presheaf was already a sheaf. Choose the covering and finite free presentations from hL. On an object mapping to a member of this covering, the basis and coordinate morphisms give finite dual bases on sections. For any finite system of constant-coefficient relations in L, write its images in M in those basis coordinates. Intersect the covering sieves lifting these finitely many coordinates through the scalar sheafification unit. Lift the restricted basis elements back to L using the adjunction unit isomorphism. The resulting scalar matrix expresses the restricted original sections in those lifted basis elements. Applying the coordinate morphisms to the original relations shows that the scalar matrix satisfies the required equations after passage to the ring sheaf. Local injectivity of its scalar unit, followed by another finite intersection of covering sieves, makes all those equations hold in Λ itself. Thus L has locally trivial relations. Apply the fixed-coefficient local relation criterion for flatness. Finite Λ is Noetherian; empty bases, empty relation matrices and the zero ring require no exception.

proof_origin.place: Section Flat modules, lemma-flat-eq (Tag 08FC); finite local bases and local bijectivity of the constant-ring sheafification unit. Direct local-relations proof, P9, 2026-10-22.
